papers.title: Sleep Homeostasis Has Circaseptan and Circatrigintan Cycles Over Year-Long Timescales.
papers.summary: Using continuous subscalp EEG in 20 healthy adults over 12–15 months, this study characterized long-term sleep homeostatic dynamics via the nightly rate of decline in slow-wave activity (0.5–4 Hz). SWA slope was predominantly negative and stable across sex and age, and continuous wavelet transform analysis revealed significant circaseptan (~7-day) and circatrigintan (~28-day) rhythmicity in most subjects.

papers.title: DPYD links glial lipids and myelination to sleep duration
papers.summary: Across mouse, zebrafish, Drosophila, and human genetic data, this study shows that DPYD and its orthologs act in glia to promote sleep through regulation of brain lipids, with loss reducing myelination and sleep independently of uracil catabolism. Manipulating myelination in zebrafish was sufficient to perturb sleep duration, and a human GWAS sleep variant was localized to a conserved oligodendrocyte-specific cis-regulatory element contacting the DPYD promoter.

papers.title: Standard touchscreen test procedures shift circadian rhythms in mice: a modified protocol to minimize circadian confounds
papers.summary: After observing circadian phase shifting in mice tested with standard touchscreen procedures during the early dark period, this study attributed the shift to light emitted by the touchscreen chambers, which induced a ~3.5 h phase delay after 7 consecutive training days. Testing 10 modified lighting conditions, the authors provide protocol recommendations that minimize circadian confounds without impairing visual discrimination or TUNL task performance.

papers.title: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation promotes local slow oscillation train initiation and persistence in elderly adults
papers.summary: Investigated whether closed-loop acoustic stimulation (CLAS) alters slow oscillation (SO) temporal organization in elderly adults by comparing stimulated (n=16) and sham (n=11) nights. Locally, CLAS reduced isolated SOs and increased consecutive SOs, train-initiation probability, and mean train length, with weaker but directionally consistent global overnight effects.

papers.title: Circadian multimodal physiological, ocular and behavioural data from a 40-hour forced-desynchrony protocol
papers.summary: This paper presents a multimodal dataset from 12 healthy adults who completed a 40-hour ultra-short forced-desynchrony protocol (2 h 30 min wake in dim light, 1 h 15 min sleep in darkness, 3 h 45 min ultradian cycle) to decouple circadian and homeostatic influences. Repeated wake-interval assessments included chromatic temporal contrast sensitivity, pupillometry, optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure, psychomotor vigilance, salivary hormones, actigraphy, ECG, temperature, blood pressure, and interstitial glucose.

papers.title: What Are Recent Insights Into Pontomedullary Circuits Controlling in REM Sleep?
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent findings on neurochemically defined pontomedullary circuits controlling REM sleep, highlighting glutamatergic Crhbp+ sublaterodorsal tegmental nucleus neurons and their reciprocal excitatory loop with dorsomedial medullary Nos1+ neurons as a core circuit for REM initiation and maintenance. It also describes projections mediating REM atonia via ventromedial medulla inhibitory neurons and separate groups triggering rapid eye movements and phasic phenomena.

papers.title: A hypothalamo-septo-hippocampal circuit for REM sleep-dependent consolidation of social memory
papers.summary: Identified a lateral supramammillary nucleus (SuM)-medial septum (MS) projection selectively active during REM sleep; REM-specific optogenetic silencing impaired consolidation of social and contextual fear memories, while silencing the downstream MS-CA2 pathway selectively disrupted social memory. Establishes a hypothalamo-septo-hippocampal (lateral SuM-MS-CA2) circuit dedicated to REM sleep-dependent social memory consolidation.

papers.title: The Hypothalamic Paraventricular Nucleus as an Integrative Hub of Circadian Regulation and a Therapeutic Target in Disease.
papers.summary: Reviews the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) as a downstream integrative node receiving SCN temporal signals and coordinating neuroendocrine, autonomic, and central outputs underlying HPA axis activity, glucose metabolism, feeding, nociception, and cardiovascular function, with cell-type-specific clock programs. Evaluates timed drug delivery, meal timing, light exposure, and PVN-focused interventions, noting limited direct human evidence of PVN clock or SCN-PVN dysfunction.

papers.title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
papers.summary: Describes the rationale and design of PD-CogT-Sleep, a double-blind randomized sham-controlled trial combining remotely delivered digital cognitive training with phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) to enhance deep sleep in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment. Primary outcome is executive function, with cognitive, patient-reported, blood biomarker, and high-density sleep EEG outcomes assessed at baseline, five weeks, and 3-month follow-up in 50 planned participants.

papers.title: Photoentrainment as Bayesian Inference: How the central circadian clock may weight and integrate the intensity and wavelength of natural light to estimate astronomical time
papers.summary: Presents a Bayesian model in which the central circadian clock predicts distributions of light intensity and spectral composition given time of day and adjusts phase according to prediction error weighted by relative reliability. Using natural light data from 59 human observers and 100 days of spectral measurements, shows how light variability across the day can generate the canonical phase response curve shape.

papers.title: Response to "From spectral parameterization to spectral staging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder".
papers.summary: This is an author response to a commentary on spectral parameterization and spectral staging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder; the abstract provides no scientific findings.

papers.title: Transient Alerting Effects of Karolinska Sleepiness Scale Ratings on Physiological and Driving Performance Indicators.
papers.summary: Pooled data from five driving simulator studies (83 participants) to test whether Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS) ratings produce transient alerting effects. Immediately after rating, blink duration and lateral position variability decreased, blink closing velocity and heart rate increased, and parietal alpha power decreased, with transient durations ranging from 40 s to beyond 120 s depending on the indicator.

papers.title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Building Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Electroencephalography.
papers.summary: This review argues that clinical translation of EEG-based AI should be judged by evidence strength rather than classification accuracy alone, examining issues such as target validity, data leakage, confounding, external validation, and clinically aligned metrics. It advocates for biologically plausible, externally generalizable, clinician-understandable systems evaluated in human-machine workflows.

papers.title: Circadian feeding rhythm loss drives sex-specific β-cell dysfunction in diet-induced obesity
papers.summary: In male and female C57BL/6 mice fed a high-fat diet for eight weeks, diet-induced obesity disrupted circadian feeding rhythms and abolished circadian glucose tolerance and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in males but not females; in male islets, circadian-regulated transcripts were reduced by 42.1%, and dark-phase time-restricted feeding restored circadian glucose tolerance, insulin secretion, and islet gene expression.

papers.title: Triphasic waves in leptomeningeal metastases and cycling alternating pattern of encephalopathy during sleep.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: Case report of a 69-year-old woman with leptomeningeal metastases from breast cancer whose EEG showed nearly continuous triphasic waves that disappeared during spontaneous sleep and recurred periodically. The sleep-linked cyclic alternating pattern of encephalopathy (CAPE) supported an encephalopathic rather than ictal interpretation, avoiding misdiagnosis of nonconvulsive status epilepticus.

papers.title: Neuropeptide signaling in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: Receptor biology, mechanistic links, and a cautious prevention framework.
papers.summary: This review integrates clinical and translational evidence for substance P/neurokinin-1, neuropeptide Y, orexin-A, and VIP/PACAP pathways in perioperative neurocognitive disorders, distinguishing established perioperative risk factors and delirium phenotyping from limited direct evidence that neuropeptide pathways cause or predict PND. It proposes a prevention framework spanning preoperative brain-reserve assessment, intraoperative neurovascular protection, and postoperative restoration of sleep, mobility, and orientation.

papers.title: How Circadian Rhythms Shape Emotional Reactivity and Regulation: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that circadian misalignment, including evening chronotype, social jet lag, and shift work, is associated with greater negative affect, impaired emotion regulation, and increased psychiatric symptoms. It highlights methodological inconsistencies and recommends combining subjective reports with physiological markers, longitudinal designs, and circadian-informed interventions.

papers.title: CircaVal: a gene-centric multi-omics platform for exploring circadian regulatory features.
papers.summary: The authors developed CircaVal, a gene-centric multi-omics platform integrating harmonized public datasets in humans, mice, and baboons to explore circadian regulatory features, introducing an integrated rhythmicity score (IRS) that combines concordance across rhythm-detection methods with cross-dataset reproducibility.

papers.title: Adolescent environmental enrichment prevents early-life stress-induced schizophrenia-like phenotypes via restoration of CREB-BDNF-TrkB signaling.
papers.summary: In a maternal separation model of early-life stress, adolescent environmental enrichment prevented schizophrenia-like behavioral and cognitive deficits in association with reversal of hippocampal oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, apoptosis, and synaptic deficits, and restoration of CREB-BDNF-TrkB signaling; pharmacological TrkB activation rescued synaptic deficits in vitro, TrkB inhibition abolished EE benefits in vivo, and TrkB levels were reduced in neuron-derived exosomes from schizophrenia patients (AUC = 0.784).

papers.title: Respiratory self-similarity is a sleep apnea endotype that predicts cardiovascular disease related mortality.
papers.summary: In secondary analyses of the Sleep Heart Health Study and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, high respiratory self-similarity (a marker of high loop gain) was associated with incident CVD (HR 1.693 in MESA; HR 1.240 in SHHS) and CVD mortality (HR 1.429 and 1.176), associations that were more apparent in men and attenuated with continuous age adjustment.

papers.title: Protocol for cell-type-specific circadian bioluminescence recording from mouse gut muscularis externa explants.
papers.summary: Describes a protocol for generating intestinal cell-type-specific PER2::CBG-LUC reporter mice, preparing longitudinal muscle-myenteric plexus explants, and performing long-term bioluminescence recording with a photomultiplier-based photon counting system. The protocol includes analysis of circadian phase and rhythmicity and verification that ex vivo rhythms reflect the endogenous in vivo circadian phase.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of extending outpatient EEG to record sleep - A retrospective study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 1762 extended (~40–50 min) outpatient EEGs without sleep deprivation, N2 sleep was achieved in 70.5% of patients, rising with recording duration, and sleep added unique interictal epileptiform discharges beyond wakefulness (29% vs. an additional 12%), with higher yield particularly in idiopathic generalized epilepsy and self-limited epilepsies.

papers.title: The relevance of sleep and chronopsychology in understanding maladaptive behaviors in eating disorders: A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that delayed sleep timing, eveningness, insomnia, and circadian misalignment co-occur with disordered eating across anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, orthorexia, and night eating syndrome, with overlapping reward-driven and neuroendocrine mechanisms; preliminary chronotherapeutic interventions (light exposure, sleep phase modification) remain insufficiently tested.

papers.title: Weighted co-expression reveals early circadian and metabolic dysregulation in precystic kidneys.
papers.summary: Applied cross-species weighted gene co-expression network analysis to renal transcriptomes from inducible Pkd1-knockout mice across precystic and cystic stages, projecting expression onto 347 curated rat kidney modules. Twenty-one of 42 transcriptionally active modules were already deregulated in the morphologically normal precystic phase, with early circadian regulator and sterol biosynthesis activation and repressed mitochondrial/oxidative-phosphorylation modules.

papers.title: The Effects of Environmental Enrichment on the Behavior of Laboratory Zebrafish (Danio rerio).
papers.summary: Assessed how three enrichment regimes (plastic plants, toys, photos of gravel) versus standard housing affected aggression, reproduction, and growth in adult laboratory zebrafish. Each enrichment treatment significantly reduced mirror-test aggression versus controls; egg production decreased after gravel treatment and egg survival increased after plant treatment, with no significant growth effects and no enrichment effect during overnight breeding.

papers.title: GraTED: Graph--Tensor EEG Decoding for Passenger Hazard Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.summary: Proposed GraTED, a graph-tensor EEG decoding model that represents electrode locations as an undirected graph and uses graph convolution plus low-rank tensor classification to preserve spatial and time-feature structure for passenger risk prediction and danger identification in autonomous vehicles. On the 11-participant, 45-hour PassengerEEG dataset, GraTED achieved the highest balanced accuracy across all three evaluation settings while using the fewest learnable parameters among seven baselines.

papers.title: Supporting the driver's perception cognition action loop using an embodied intelligent cockpit framework for explainable fatigue intervention.
papers.summary: Evaluated an embodied intelligent cockpit framework combining multimodal fatigue detection (EEG, eye tracking, vehicle dynamics), SHAP-based feature attribution, and LLM-generated state-specific auditory feedback in 40 drivers during simulated conditional automated driving. Explanatory speech yielded a 0.192-s shorter mean braking reaction time and 0.085-m lower SDLP versus generic speech; retrospective leave-one-subject-out AUC was 0.85.

papers.title: Autonomic Reactivity and EEG-defined Clusters Reveal Distinct Chronic Pain Profiles.
papers.summary: In 177 patients with chronic pain after spine surgery, integrating stress-related heart rate variability (HRV) with resting-state EEG features revealed two EEG clusters and a nominally significant HRV-by-EEG interaction (p=0.030) on pain scores, with higher pain in the LF/HF-decrease group within one EEG cluster; findings were exploratory and require validation.

papers.title: BMAL1-Sleep interactions modulate quality of life in allergic rhinitis patients with circadian dysregulation.
papers.summary: Compared 100 allergic rhinitis patients with 33 healthy controls on chronotype, sleep quality, quality of life, and peripheral leukocyte circadian CLOCK gene expression. Patients showed poorer sleep, more evening chronotypes, and dysregulated CLOCK/PER1/BMAL1/CRY1 expression, with BMAL1 expression positively correlated with RQLQ scores and interacting with sleep duration on activity limitations and sleep efficiency on nasal symptoms.

papers.title: Neural and behavioral signatures of live and video demonstrations in bimanual interpersonal coordination: An EEG and kinematic study.
papers.summary: Examined how live versus video modeling and execution versus observation shape mu (8-12 Hz) and high-beta (21-30 Hz) EEG activity and kinematic coordination in 20 right-handed females performing a bimanual interpersonal coordination task. Mu and high-beta desynchronized during execution, and live-model interaction produced stronger high-beta suppression and more stable kinematic coupling than video modeling, while mu suppression during observation increased across practice phases.

papers.title: Intraoperative electroencephalography burst suppression during endoscopic third ventriculostomy: Case report and implications for neuromonitoring.
papers.summary: Case report of a 28-year-old woman undergoing endoscopic third ventriculostomy for obstructive hydrocephalus in whom endoscope insertion and ventricular irrigation provoked two episodes of tachycardic hypertensive crisis coinciding with bilateral EEG burst suppression; hemodynamics normalized within 15 min but EEG recovery took 55 min. The authors suggest processed intraoperative EEG may serve as an early sign of acute cerebral disturbance, while noting its added value remains unproven.

papers.title: Probable Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder Associated With Escitalopram in a Patient With Schizoaffective Disorder: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Reports a 46-year-old man with schizoaffective disorder who developed probable REM sleep behavior disorder (dream enactment, sleep paralysis, daytime sleepiness) about 14 months after starting escitalopram 5 mg, with episodes resolving after escitalopram withdrawal and clonazepam initiation and no recurrence at later follow-up.

papers.title: In-person UCLA-PEERS® program for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder in Italy: study protocol for a pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial with pragmatic features and exploratory EEG markers of treatment response.
papers.summary: Protocol for a two-arm pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing in-person UCLA PEERS® with treatment as usual in 36 Italian adolescents with autism spectrum disorder Level 1, with primary focus on feasibility (recruitment, retention, attendance, fidelity) and exploratory clinical outcomes including social functioning. Baseline EEG N400 congruency effect during a gesture-word integration task will be explored as a marker of treatment response.

papers.title: Immunometabolic reprogramming: a working framework for disease development, endotype differentiation, and therapeutic considerations in pediatric asthma.
papers.summary: This review integrates evidence on immunometabolic reprogramming in pediatric asthma and proposes a "Metabolic Latching Model" in which early-life insults establish persistent inflammatory memory through metabolism-epigenetic coupling. It prioritizes testable hypotheses on monocyte glycolytic baseline predicting wheeze-to-asthma transition, metabolic intervention in obese asthma, and the HDAC2-GSH/butyrate axis in steroid sensitivity.

papers.title: Noise Pollution in Cement Manufacturing Industries: A Comprehensive Review of Environmental and Occupational Health Impacts and Mitigation Strategies.
papers.summary: Reviews literature on noise pollution from cement manufacturing, reporting continuous workplace and community sound levels of about 68.8-103.3 dB(A) generated by crushing, grinding, and heating, and linking exposure to hearing loss, cardiovascular problems, sleep disorders, and stress in workers plus behavioral and habitat effects on animals. Concludes that a hierarchy of engineering, administrative, and spatial controls is effective but constrained by cost and inconsistent regulation, with evidence mostly from cross-sectional single-factory studies lacking longitudinal data.

papers.title: Rivastigmine and Emerging Nanotechnological Strategies for Targeted Delivery: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.summary: This review summarizes nanotechnological strategies for targeted delivery of rivastigmine in Alzheimer's disease, including liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, dendrimers, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, nano-emulsions, and mesoporous silica nanoparticles aimed at improving drug loading, blood-brain barrier penetration, and controlled release while reducing off-target effects. It also reports observed positive off-target effects such as improved appetite and possible benefit in colitis, while calling for mechanistic studies to justify repurposing.

papers.title: The quiet end of the spectrum: A case report and review of "simple schizophrenia".
papers.journal: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
papers.summary: This case report with focused narrative review describes a 24-year-old woman with a two-year insidious decline in motivation, social engagement, and cognition with affective flattening, avolition, and psychomotor slowing but no hallucinations or delusions; after excluding organic pathology and refractoriness to antidepressants, antipsychotics, and ECT, schizophrenia was diagnosed. The authors argue current diagnostic systems may overlook schizophrenia without hallucinations or delusions and that neuropsychiatric markers and cognitive trajectories may enable earlier identification.

papers.title: Sphenoidal Meningioma with Focal Seizures Masquerading as Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome in HIV Patient.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 47-year-old woman with HIV who developed recurrent focal-onset seizures evolving to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures about four weeks after starting antiretroviral therapy, initially suggesting immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome, but imaging revealed a 3.0 × 4.3 cm left sphenoid wing meningioma. Gross total surgical resection achieved seizure freedom at 12 months, highlighting the need for a broad differential diagnosis and integration of clinical, electrophysiological, infectious, and imaging data in adults with HIV.

papers.title: Revamped transposon-induced hepatocellular carcinoma model reveals deep similarities of cancer-driver landscapes across mice and humans
papers.summary: Developed 3xfOnc3, a three-frame Sleeping Beauty transposon mutagenesis system, and tested it in mouse liver, where 60% of mice developed heterogeneous hepatocellular tumors within 12 months. Background-corrected analysis prioritized 315 driver candidates (243 protein-coding), showed multiclonal context-dependent clonal expansion, and found candidate orthologues enriched for Cancer Gene Census genes and pan-cancer mutations.

papers.title: An integrative view of human nociceptor diversity: from microneurography to molecular identity.
papers.summary: This review integrates functional and molecular approaches to study human nociceptor diversity, discussing how microneurography-defined biophysical hallmarks can be transferred to in vitro patch-clamp paradigms and combined with Patch-seq to assign molecular identities to functionally defined nociceptor subtypes, such as mechano-insensitive 'sleeping' nociceptors. It highlights multimodal datasets linking electrophysiology, transcriptomics, and computational modeling to uncover ion channel mechanisms underlying pathological firing in neuropathic pain.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
